subject: Medivista trial charter + evaluation pathway
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Hawkins <matt.hawkins@medivista.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-18T15:10:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap + suggested trial charter (next steps)

Hi Matt —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap to make sure we’re aligned and to propose a lightweight trial charter so your team can evaluate Redwood without disrupting current flows. Please correct anything I’ve mis-stated.

Discovery highlights (from today):
- Primary goal: reduce document-processing latency and cost for clinical coding workflows (batch + shadow use cases).
- Key success metric: 95% of high-confidence codes returned within 2s (online shadow), and batch throughput of ~10k docs/hour with median latency <350ms per doc for offline runs.
- Data: you can provide a 4-week sample of de-identified records and a static holdout (~2k records) for scoring.
- Security: SOC 2 + HIPAA compliance are prerequisites; procurement will request an attestation and an architecture diagram.

Suggested trial charter (proposed, 4 weeks):
1) Kickoff week (1): finalize access and data-sharing SOW, exchange sample data, create test endpoints (private tenant).
2) Shadow & offline parallel runs (weeks 2–3):
   - Shadow: route a 10% sample of production traffic through Redwood for real-time comparison (no writes to prod).
   - Offline: run full sample in batch and compute quality metrics against your gold labels.
3) Evaluation week (4): score against success criteria, run a short session to walk results with your ops and data science teams.

Ownership:
- Redwood: tech onboarding, endpoints, trial monitoring, and a simple eval dashboard. (Marissa will own the trial ops.)
- Medivista: provide data samples, define acceptance thresholds, procurement lead on contract items (Aisha).

Evaluation methodology discussion: we recommend a hybrid approach — primarily offline graded runs for statistical rigor, plus a short online shadow window to validate latency and real-world behavior. I’ve attached a baseline eval matrix (CSV) and a trial charter doc for your team to review.

Next steps:
- You confirm procurement contact and timing (I noted Aisha + procurement@medivista.com).
- If approved, propose a Thu 7/22 10am ET kickoff.
- Marissa will send a detailed tech checklist and access playbook.

Thanks — happy to tighten any items.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment stubs: Medivista_trial_charter_v1.docx (docx, 48KB), eval-matrix-csv.csv (csv, 6KB)

From: Matt Hawkins <matt.hawkins@medivista.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@medivista.com>, procurement@medivista.com
Date: 2026-07-18T20:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + suggested trial charter (next steps)

Karthik —

Thanks for the thorough recap. That aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Success metrics: the 95% within 2s for high-confidence sounds good, but we’ll need to define how we bucket confidence and which code sets are in scope (ICD-10 primary codes only initially).
2) Data: we can share a de-identified 4-week sample by EOD Friday; holdout set will be ready next Monday.
3) Shadow: we want the shadow window limited to a single business day to start (not continuous 2 weeks) — operationally easier. Batch runs are the priority for acceptance.
4) Procurement: Aisha is handling contract review; they’ll want a data flow diagram and SOC 2 report.

I’m good for the Thu 7/22 10am ET kickoff — put Marissa on the invite and loop in procurement if they have contract questions.

—Matt
VP Engineering, Medivista Health
matt.hawkins@medivista.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Hawkins <matt.hawkins@medivista.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-19T02:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + suggested trial charter (next steps)

Great — appreciate the clarifications. Adjusting the charter per your notes:

- Scope: ICD-10 primary codes only for the initial batch evaluation. We’ll add confidence-bucket definitions to the eval spec (High: model confidence >= 0.85; Medium: 0.6–0.85; Low: <0.6) so acceptance gates are explicit.
- Shadow window: we'll do a 1-business-day shadow run to validate latency and routing — Marissa will own scheduling and monitoring.
- Batch: run full 4-week sample in our offline pipeline; we’ll compute precision/recall and the per-code latency distribution.
- Deliverables before kickoff:
   1) Trial charter doc (attached) — includes timeline and roles.
   2) Eval matrix CSV with scoring weights by code criticality.
   3) Security packet: SOC 2 summary + network diagram (we’ll share a redacted diagram for the private tenant).

I’ve tentatively booked Thu 2026-07-22 10:00–11:00 ET and will send a calendar invite once Marissa confirms the tech checklist. If procurement needs to pre-sign an NDA or send a PO, loop them on this thread.

Quick ask for you (to keep the kickoff productive): can you confirm the internal stakeholders who should attend (data science lead + ops lead)? We’ll invite the same.

Thanks — Karthik

Attachment stubs: Medivista_trial_charter_v1.docx, eval-matrix-csv.csv, security-summary.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Hawkins <matt.hawkins@medivista.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@medivista.com>
Date: 2026-07-22T19:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + suggested trial charter (next steps)

Thanks everyone — quick logistics update before the kickoff tomorrow:

1) Tech checklist: Matt, please share SFTP creds (or a secure Drive link) for the de-identified sample. If you prefer, we can accept data via the secure upload link I’ll include in the invite.
2) Evaluation rubric highlights (so your data team can review ahead):
   - Primary acceptance gate: batch precision@top1 >= 0.88 across the gold set, with no more than 6% catastrophic failures (wrong primary code) on high-priority code groups.
   - Latency gate for shadow day: median p50 < 350ms, p95 < 1200ms for requests within the private tenant.
   - Qualitative: ops-runbook completeness and retraining handoff notes.
3) Roles: Marissa (trial ops) + Ben (evaluation lead) for Redwood. Laura is copied for executive visibility.

I’ve attached the final trial charter doc and a populated eval-matrix CSV. See you all tomorrow 10am ET.

Best,
Marissa
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
